references.text: God makes a distinction between the Egyptians and the Israelites by sparing the land of Goshen from the plagues, showing the same pattern of light for Israel while Egypt is in darkness.
The land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was spared from the plague of hail, demonstrating God's protection over His people just as the light shone in their dwellings.
The cloud brought darkness for the Egyptians but light at night for the Israelites, a similar motif highlighting the contrast between darkness and light.
For God, darkness is not dark, and the night shines like the day. This reveals God's power over both light and darkness.
Darkness covers the earth and the peoples, but the Lord's glory rises over Israel. The same contrast between darkness for the nations and light for God's people.
The wicked wander in darkness and do not know what they stumble over, while the path of the righteous is like a shining light.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it. John uses the light/darkness motif also found in Exodus.

Jesus says, 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.' Cross-reference to the contrast between light for God's people and darkness for others.
God has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of His beloved Son. Thematically linked to deliverance from darkness in Egypt.
A parallel between three days of blindness/darkness as a divine intervention: judgment on the enemy (Egypt) versus a path of repentance for Paul.
Theological parallel about selective revelation: witnesses see the light but do not understand the message, while the chosen one (Paul/Israel) receives full experience.
